learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of parameters, references, and reusable queries and identify when it is useful.
Apply the lesson pattern to a small Excel example using the stated assumptions.

content.intro: This lesson covers Parameters, References, and Reusable Queries as part of Power Query and Data Preparation. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Parameters, References, and Reusable Queries supports repeatable analysis by organizing, cleaning, summarizing, or relating data. Preserve the raw source and reconcile a summary back to its input records. Compatibility: Power Query, the Data Model, Power Pivot and DAX are related but distinct capabilities; their exact availability varies by Excel edition, operating system, license and update channel. Follow the course’s local availability checklist before building a dependent workflow.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Parameters, References, and Reusable Queries focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Query references; Parameters; Function-based transformations; Reusing and organizing query steps. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: A Power Query M transformation changes OrderDate to date and Amount to currency types, assuming these source column names exist.
content_blocks.run_instructions: In Excel, use Data → Get Data to open Power Query Editor; replace Source with the actual prior step and verify locale-sensitive dates and currency values before loading.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for parameters, references, and reusable queries. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates parameters, references, and reusable queries. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates parameters, references, and reusable queries; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: A Power Query M transformation changes OrderDate to date and Amount to currency types, assuming these source column names exist.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Parameters, References, and Reusable Queries supports the workflow in Power Query and Data Preparation.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
